subject: Packrat project still sees system library, not isolated

messages.author: 4466c992e65f1ad8
messages.subject: Packrat project still sees system library, not isolated
parts:
Hi,

I am experimenting with packrat for the first time.  This is extremely useful when using R code in production.  

I have setup and bootstrapped a new packrat project.  However, I am still able to access libraries that were installed outside the project.  I think it is because packrat still goes to my user library to search for packages

.libPaths()
[1] "/Users/jeffreyw/packrat-test/library/x86_64-apple-darwin10.8.0/3.0.2"
[2] "/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.0/Resources/library"

Shouldn't it only be able to access the first library? 

The .Rprofile file that gets added to the packrat project has this line

.libPaths(localLib)

which according to the documentation for .libPaths will only append the local packrat library to the already existing user library.

I think the .Renviron command R_LIBS_SITE="::: no r_libs_site ;;;" is supposed to wipe out references to the user library, but when I start R the variable .Library, which is used to populate .libPaths, still exists

> .Library
[1] "/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/library"

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Packrat project still sees system library, not isolated
parts:
I think we forgot to document this problem, sorry.

TL;DR: CRAN R for Mac is weird, use this script to fix it: https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/8441049

We have to keep the system library (/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.0/Resources/library) in the libpath because it contains the base packages, which we don't bring into your packrat library. However, the default CRAN build of R for Mac sets up permissions on the system library in such a way that user-installed packages will also go there. That's a problem, since we want to be isolated from those.

On other platforms, you don't have this problem; each user has their own personal package library, and install.packages uses it by default. Only when actually installing as root (or sudo) will you end up in a system-wide library (and at least for Linux, even in that case it's a separate library than base/recommended, which packrat knows how to exclude).

The good news is that if you tighten up the permissions on your system library, then R will start behaving as we want it to; it'll create a personal package library for you and start installing stuff there. And then packrat will do the right thing, removing the personal package library from the libpath.

But that doesn't help you with the non-base, non-recommended packages that are still in the system library. What you want to do there is move out all of those packages into the personal package library.

I've written a script that 1) backs up your system library (just in case), 2) creates a personal package library, 3) moves any non-base non-recommended packages from the system library to your personal package library, and 4) tightens up the permissions on the system library so that only root can write to it. The upshot is that you will correctly be isolated from all but base and recommended packages, which is how packrat is designed to run.

You can easily run the script with this command (sorry about the wrapping, it should all be on one line):

curl https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/8441049/raw/cbe90a0c1eef2443acc1dcafeff6741e3a78e029/mac_r_userlib.sh | bash -e

messages.author: 1a7505f6457dcfbd
messages.subject: Re: Packrat project still sees system library, not isolated
parts:
Hi Joe,

Thank you so much for all the support and great work that you, and the other guys, are giving to the R community.

In fact in Debian there are no troubles with the system and user libraries but on mac I had to run your script. Somehow your command didn't work out but it worked with:

cd ~/
wget https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/8441049/raw/cbe90a0c1eef2443acc1dcafeff6741e3a78e029/mac_r_userlib.sh
sudo chmod 755 ~/mac_r_userlib.sh
./mac_r_userlib.sh

Keep on the good work!

BTW, good talk at Vimeo.

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: Packrat project still sees system library, not isolated
parts:
Hi Antonio,

In the newer versions of packrat we do work around this problem -- packrat projects using the latest version of packrat should no longer require this migration script.

(for the interested -- we now symlink the 'base' and 'recommended' packages into a pseudo-system library, and force the R session to view that pseudo-system library as the true system library, isolating us from other packages installed in the system library.)

Cheers,
Kevin
